alignments.note: Anarthrous dative; the case preposition unto stays with the noun (rules 21, 23).
Participle; the ASV reorders it before the agent phrase (rule 15).
The English preposition realizes the Greek preposition (rule 36).

Genitive rendered on + noun phrase; the case preposition rides with the noun (rules 21, 23). One Greek noun rendered by an English modifier plus noun: doers glosses the -ποιός element rather than completing it generically, so rule 66 heads on doers.
The repeated for is an ordinary helper on the second conjunct, the one εἰς being aligned to the first (rules 7, 40).

Substantival adjective with no Greek article: the supplied to them that and the case preposition are helpers on the one source word (rules 7, 21, 23). Head follows the parallel κακοποιῶν → evil doers of this same verse, do glossing the -ποιός element; a head on well is defensible (rules 17, 66).
